name: D
note: C-family systems language aiming to fix C++'s pitfalls
typeSystem: Static, strong, C-family syntax with type inference (auto), templates/generics, and transitive const, immutable, and shared qualifiers. These support thread isolation and explicit synchronisation, although strict rejection of individual unsynchronised shared accesses currently requires the preview nosharedaccess option.
runtime: Compiled ahead-of-time to native code; garbage-collected by default, but supports manual memory management and @nogc code for systems-level use.

runtimes.name: Native (DMD, LDC, GDC)
runtimes.role: Multiple independent native-code compilers target the same D language specification.

compilers.name: DMD
compilers.role: The reference D compiler, from the D Language Foundation.

compilers.name: LDC
compilers.role: LLVM-based D compiler, good for optimised release builds and cross-compilation.

compilers.name: GDC
compilers.role: GCC-based D compiler, benefiting from GCC's back-end optimisations and target support.

concurrencyModel: Message-passing between threads via std.concurrency (spawn plus typed messages, in the spirit of Erlang), plus lower-level shared-memory threading. Mutable globals are thread-local by default; cross-thread mutable data is marked shared and requires explicit synchronisation, atomics, or stricter preview checking.
